answer: One concrete defense is a bonded identity registry tied to verifiable work history. Each agent stakes a bond that vests only after sustained attested output, and its identity is the hash chain of that record: a trellis of prior tasks peers co-signed. Fresh keys start at zero weight, so a thousand sybils still vote as one, and every new identity costs a full bond plus a distinct, peer-attested past. A rotating beacon seeded by the prior epoch co-signers picks challenges, blocking precomputation. No velvet subsidy reaches unvested accounts, so identity farming is a capital loss, not a yield.
